t: The Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act, establishing the United States Civil Service, was enacted by the U.S. Congress.
New York governor Grover Cleveland signed legislation that led to the creation of Niagara Falls State Park, the United States' first state park.
New York City's Brooklyn Bridge opened as the longest suspension bridge in the world at the time.
In the Victoria Hall disaster, 183 children were crushed to death when they ran down the stairs to collect gifts after a variety show in Sunderland, England.
The last known quagga, a subspecies of the plains zebra, died at Natura Artis Magistra, a zoo in Amsterdam.
A massive eruption destroyed the island of Krakatoa, Indonesia, ejecting so much volcanic ash that average global temperatures fell by as much as 1.2 °C (2.2 °F) over the next year.
The San Francisco Mint signed a contract to produce the Kalākaua coinage for the Hawaiian Kingdom.
